evidence/construct_nulls_legality_aware..why_it_matters: E-CAL is the CORRECTED legality-aware calibration -- the paper's central fix, described in its own appendix as 'the single machine-readable source for these nine rows'. A reviewer following the pointer in the frozen artifact does not find it.

WHAT_THE_ARTIFACT_SHIPS_INSTEAD.status: SUPERSEDED. construct_nulls_legality_aware.json names it, with sha256 275112623d0574068..., in its own 'supersedes' field.
WHAT_THE_ARTIFACT_SHIPS_INSTEAD.consequence: the frozen artifact contains the record the paper argues is WRONG (it used a null MMLU-Pro cannot produce) and omits the record that replaced it. That is worse than an absence: a reviewer who opens the artifact finds a calibration whose numbers the manuscript has retracted.

WHY_IT_RECURRED.root_cause: identical to PACKAGING_DEFECT_20260816.md: the freeze manifest is hand-enumerated. submission_complete was frozen to repair the first instance and correctly restored the 10 files named at that time -- but the calibration fix landed 2026-08-16 14:13, AFTER that freeze, so the new E-CAL target was never added.

timeline.gap: the artifact predates the fix it is supposed to document

WHY_IT_RECURRED.the_general_lesson: A hand-enumerated manifest is not repaired by enumerating more paths; it is repaired by deriving the manifest from the manuscript. Every evidence change re-opens the same hole, and the second instance looks exactly like the first.

REMEDY_IMPLEMENTED.what_it_does: extracts every \texttt{evidence/...} and \texttt{code/...} path from sections/*.tex, rejoins the ones LaTeX line-breaking splits across adjacent \texttt groups, and asserts each resolves inside the frozen submission
REMEDY_IMPLEMENTED.measured: 17 cited paths, 15 present, 2 missing, 0 unresolved fragments
REMEDY_IMPLEMENTED.parsing_note: a naive extraction reported 4 additional 'missing' paths that were line-break fragments of my own making (evidence/mmlu_scale_, code/mmlu_pro_, ...). The rejoin step removes all four. A gate that cries wolf on its own parsing gets ignored, so this was fixed before the verdict was trusted.
REMEDY_IMPLEMENTED.scope_limit: PRESENCE only. A stale file at the right path passes this gate. It does not check content, hashes, or freshness.

WHAT_I_AM_NOT_DOING: I am not re-freezing the artifact in this pass. The meta-review's own ordering is to fix the calibration FIRST and repackage after, and the calibration work is still open (BH q-column, denominator corrections, and the count gates all landed today). Re-freezing now would produce a third snapshot that goes stale the next time an evidence file changes. The gate makes the staleness visible so the eventual re-freeze can be verified rather than asserted.
